test.title: Section 2 · leaving a job and the company pension

topic.en: Two workplace texts: notice and the last weeks before leaving, and the company pension scheme.
topic.kk: Екі жұмыс мәтіні: жұмыстан кетер алдындағы ескерту мерзімі мен соңғы апталар, компанияның зейнетақы бағдарламасы.
topic.ru: Два рабочих текста: срок уведомления и последние недели перед уходом, корпоративная пенсионная программа.

textTitles: Leaving the company: notice and your last weeks

texts.label: A
texts.title: Leaving the company: notice and your last weeks

paragraphs.text: Leaving the company: notice and your last weeks. If you decide to leave, you must give notice in writing to your manager. The length of notice depends on your contract: one week for staff in their probation period, one month for most permanent staff and three months for managers. Your manager will confirm your last day of work in writing within five working days of receiving your notice. In some cases the company may agree to a shorter notice period, but it is not obliged to do so.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Any holiday that you have not taken by your last day will be paid in your final salary. If you have taken more holiday than you have earned so far this year, the difference will be deducted. You may be asked to use some of your remaining holiday during the notice period, particularly if your manager feels that a long notice period is not needed to hand over your work.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Before you leave, you should prepare a handover document listing the tasks you are responsible for, the progress of current projects and the contacts that your replacement will need. Your manager will agree with you who should receive this document. All company property, including your laptop, mobile phone, pass and any keys, must be returned to the facilities team on or before your last day, and the cost of items that are not returned may be deducted from your final pay.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: All leavers are invited to an exit interview with a member of the human resources team, usually in the final week. The interview is voluntary, and what you say will not be shared with your manager in a form that identifies you. Answers are collected and reviewed twice a year to help the company understand why people leave. Your final salary and a statement of your earnings for the tax year will be sent to you after the next normal pay date.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Joining the workplace pension. All employees aged between twenty-two and the state pension age who earn more than a set minimum are enrolled in the company pension scheme automatically after three months of employment. Other employees may join if they wish by completing a form on the staff website. Membership is not compulsory: anyone who has been enrolled can opt out within one month and will have any contributions they have already paid returned to them in full.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Each month, employees pay five per cent of their salary into the scheme and the company adds a further four per cent. Staff may choose to pay more than five per cent, and for every extra one per cent they pay, the company adds a further half a per cent, up to a maximum company contribution of seven per cent. Contributions are taken from salary before tax, so the real cost to the employee is lower than the amount paid in.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The money is invested by an independent pension provider, not by the company itself. New members are placed in the default fund, which spreads investments across different types of assets and gradually moves into lower-risk investments as the member approaches retirement. Members who prefer to choose for themselves can select from twelve other funds through the provider’s website, and they can change funds at any time without charge.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Anyone who leaves the company keeps the pension they have built up, and it remains invested until they reach retirement age, although they can transfer it to another scheme if they wish. Each member receives an annual statement showing the value of their pension and an estimate of what it may pay. The human resources team runs a lunchtime presentation on the scheme every three months, and members can also book a free appointment with an adviser from the provider.
paragraphs.label: D
